Subject: RE: Slower responses from Redwood API (eu) — investigation notes

Folks — brief technical summary and mitigation plan (current):

What we found:
- Root cause: an autoscaler regression in the EU hostgroup's short-request optimizer. Under certain high-concurrency, low-latency workloads the autoscaler produced many small micro-instances with suboptimal batching behavior. That created a transient backlog across mid-tier routing and resulted in p95 spikes and some request timeouts.
- Trigger window aligns with a customer traffic surge at ~07:40–07:50 UTC.

Mitigation performed (09:00 UTC):
1) Temporarily disabled the short-request autoscaler heuristic in eu-west-1 (rollback to conservative scaling). This reduced newly created micro-instances and allowed existing pooled instances to absorb traffic.
2) Forced failover of a subset of traffic to our reserved EU capacity pool (no config change required from customers).

Impact now:
- p95 has dropped from ~1.6s to ~0.42s for affected customers; timeouts are no longer increasing. We still see a small tail (~0.6% of requests) and are monitoring.

Next actions (in order):
- Apply the autoscaler patch (runbook-eu-autoscaler-rollout.patch.diff) to prevent re-introduction (RED-4532).
- Add a temporary routing rule to prefer reserved pools for low-token, high-concurrency patterns.
- Follow up with a detailed postmortem and long-term plan (change to autoscaler tests + canary ramping).

I’ll keep this thread as the incident comms channel; please surface any customer-facing text and I’ll confirm technical accuracy.

— Vivek
